      <description>To menn er pågrepet etter en voldshendelse utenfor et utested i Arendal natt til søndag.

      <description>Timon Haugan leverte med presset som leder etter første omgang og kjørte inn til seier på slalåmen i Gurgl. Han ble med det første nordmann med verdenscupseier i Gurgl.
24 år gamle Eirik Hystad Solberg overrasket stort på og ble nummer to - hans første pallplass på toppnivå.
Atle Lie McGrath var nummer to før finaleomgangen, men hektet i en port og forsvant ut. I frustrasjon kastet han stavene og ble liggende ved siden av løypa. Også Henrik Kristoffersen, som var nummer seks etter første omgang, kjørte ut i finalen.
Lucas Pinheiro Braathen jaktet sin tredje strake seier - men 26-åringen kjørte ut i første omgang.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Karoline Grøtting best av alle på sesongåpningens siste dag – skiskytter imponerte</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>
      <category>Langrenn</category>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/historisk-_gta-6_-lansering_-solgte-for-nesten-4-milliarder-dollar-pa-en-dag-1.18086187</link>
      <description>Spillgiganten Rockstar Games knuser alle rekorder, melder Variety.
Allerede på lanseringsdagen omsatte «Grand Theft Auto 6», også kjent som «GTA 6», for 3,79 milliarder dollar.
Det tilsvarer over 37 milliarder norske kroner, og spillet forbigår dermed superheltfilmen «Avengers: End Game» som den største underholdningslanseringen noensinne.
«GTA 6» ble lansert torsdag på PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X og S, i tillegg til at det kan strømmes på Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming.
I den sjette utgaven av actionspillet følger spillerne duoen Jason og Lucia mens de ufører ran og andre kriminelle oppdrag i den fiktive amerikanske delstaten Leonida.</description>

      <title>Norwegian ber 5000 kundar sperre bankkortet etter datainnbrot</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norwegian-ber-5000-kundar-sperre-bankkortet-etter-datainnbrot-1.18085456</link>
      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.
Ein skadeleg kode blei lagt inn på nettsidene til Norwegian, som gjorde at kortdetaljar som blei brukt på nettsida kan ha vore synlege i ein kortare periode måndag.
Selskapet oppdaga datainnbrotet onsdag.
Hendinga er rapportert til Datatilsynet.
I førre veke blei det kjent at 144.000 passasjerar hos Norwegian og Widerøe blei lekka i forbindelse med eit datainnbrot hos ein spansk IT-leverandør.</description>

      <title>Israel med ny offensiv – tre drept</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

   <description>Nach zwei Wochen zäher Verhandlungen ist der Klimagipfel COP31 ohne Einigung zu Ende gegangen. Damit wird der Ausstieg aus den fossilen Brennstoffen wieder fraglich. Ungelöst ist auch die Finanzierung der Klimaanpassung.</description>

]]> 1363238 Look up: International Space Station visible over Vancouver Island in coming days https://cheknews.ca/look-up-international-space-station-visible-over-vancouver-island-in-coming-days-1363233/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:13:26 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363233

Vancouver Islanders will have several opportunities to spot the International Space Station streaking across the evening sky over the next week, with some particularly bright passes expected.

The post Look up: International Space Station visible over Vancouver Island in coming days appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Vancouver Islanders will have several opportunities to spot the International Space Station streaking across the evening sky over the next week, with some particularly bright passes expected.

According to NASA’s Spot the Station website, the orbiting laboratory will be visible from several Vancouver Island communities, including Victoria, Sidney, Nanaimo, Courtenay, Port Alberni and Gold River, through early December.

The ISS orbits Earth at an altitude of approximately 400 kilometres, travelling at a speed of roughly 28,000 kilometres per hour.

Despite that distance, the station is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye, even in urban areas with significant light pollution.

It typically appears as a bright white dot moving steadily across the sky, resembling an airplane without flashing lights.

Unlike an aircraft, however, the ISS moves much faster and does not change direction as it crosses the sky.

There will be several upcoming viewing opportunities for Island communities, with passes lasting between two and seven minutes.

Some of the best opportunities are expected later this week, when the station will climb particularly high above the horizon.

For Victoria, the best viewing times are below:

Friday, Nov. 27, could offer one of the best opportunities, with the ISS expected to be visible for seven minutes and reach a maximum height of 84 degrees — almost directly overhead.

During that pass, the station is expected to first appear 10 degrees above the west-northwestern horizon before travelling across the sky and disappearing toward the east-southeast.

NASA says the best time to see the ISS is shortly before sunrise or after sunset, when sunlight reflects off the station while the sky below is dark. No telescope or binoculars are required.

The station usually appears as one of the brightest objects in the night sky after the Moon, making it relatively easy to identify when conditions are clear.

The ISS completes an orbit around Earth approximately every 90 minutes, allowing astronauts aboard to experience 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.

The station has been continuously occupied since November 2000 and serves as an orbiting laboratory for scientific research involving international partners, including Canada.

Vancouver Islanders can also check upcoming viewing opportunities for their community through NASA’s Spot the Station website.

The post Look up: International Space Station visible over Vancouver Island in coming days appeared first on CHEK.

]]> 1363233 All signs show Canada can’t meet its Paris target — here’s why Ottawa won’t admit it https://cheknews.ca/all-signs-show-canada-cant-meet-its-paris-target-heres-why-ottawa-wont-admit-it-1363229/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:39:53 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363229

All the studies suggest Canada won't meet its target. The government's own projections say it will miss it. The prime minister himself acknowledged emissions are on the rise. So why hasn't the federal government said it is no longer committed to the 2030 target?

The post All signs show Canada can’t meet its Paris target — here’s why Ottawa won’t admit it appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

In June, Prime Minister Mark Carney told Canadians that the country’s emissions would be higher “in the next few years” than previously projected. Those projections already said Canada would miss its 2030 emissions target under the Paris climate accord.

The government’s own projections — published in its emissions reductions progress report a year ago — showed a best-case scenario of a 28 per cent reduction in emissions from 2005 levels in 2030.

And that was before the Carney government introduced a suite of climate policy rollbacks over the past year, including a delay to the introduction of more stringent tailpipe emissions. That measure was supposed to take the place of the now-scrapped electric vehicle sales mandate; it won’t come into effect now until at least 2029.

Canada’s commitment under the Paris agreement was to cut emissions by between 40 to 45 per cent of 2005 levels. The government of Stephen Harper set a target of 30 per cent.

This week, Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin insisted Canada is committed to its Paris commitments. That claim earned her some public criticism from two of her predecessors while she attended the United Nations climate conference in Turkey last week.

Dabrusin wouldn’t answer when asked whether that commitment includes the 2030 target. In its public statements, the government has leaned on the target of achieving net-zero by 2050.

All the studies suggest Canada won’t meet its target. The government’s own projections say it will miss it. The prime minister himself acknowledged emissions are on the rise. So why hasn’t the federal government said it is no longer committed to the 2030 target?

“I think they’re afraid to come out and say it because it’s putting in people’s faces that they’re making a choice to make wildfires worse, to make flooding worse, to actually leave a worse world for our children,” said Keith Stewart, senior energy strategist with Greenpeace Canada.

“Julie Dabrusin seems like a very nice person. But she’s going to go down in history as the worst environment minister in Canada’s history because it’s been on her watch that Canada has rolled back environment and climate policies in a way that not even Stephen Harper attempted.”

Asked whether Dabrusin has been put in the job to defend Carney’s policy choices, Stewart said nobody is under the impression that she is “calling the shots.”

“This is clearly coming from the prime minister. But she’s at that cabinet table and she’s standing behind those decisions. And as someone who has said she’s committed to action on climate change, her other option is to resign in protest to make it clear that this is unacceptable,” Stewart said.

“If being at a cabinet table is more important to you than having the right decisions come out of the cabinet table, that’s a choice a politician can make.”

In a statement, Dabrusin’s office said Canada is “committed to its Paris agreement of achieving net-zero by 2050.” The statement did not address a direct question of whether Canada is still committed to its 2030 target.

“We cannot achieve our climate goals when we are divided,” wrote Amy Falkner, Dabrusin’s press secretary.

“Our focus is on results that unite Canadians: building major clean energy projects across the country, driving mass electrification, making significant investments in the low-carbon economy, and working in co-operation with provinces, territories and Indigenous Peoples.”

Falkner added that Canada is still committed to reporting its progress under the Net-Zero Accountability Act as required in December 2027, and will report on its 2030 target next month to the United Nations Climate Change Secretariat — as required under the Paris Agreement.

But whether the Net-Zero Accountability Act even has any teeth was the subject of debate on Parliament Hill this week. The act doesn’t set out any fines or penalties for Canada missing or abandoning its climate targets.

At Thursday’s meeting of the House of Commons environment committee, B.C. Conservative MP Ellis Ross grilled Canada’s interim environment commissioner on what purpose the act even serves.

“It seems like everybody agrees, except government, that they’re not going to meet their targets. So when the government is clearly falling short of emissions targets, and in actuality intends to expand its emissions, what exactly does the Net-Zero Accountability Act do?” Ellis asked.

“We’ve been talking about (emissions) for the better part of 20 years. But in terms of the 2030 commitments and 2050 commitments, we’re not going to meet it. So does the Net-Zero Accountability Act mean anything today?”

Elsa Da Costa, the interim environment commissioner, replied that the act was an “important tool” for her office to hold the government to account.

The Angus Reid Institute released an online poll of 1,770 Canadians in July which suggested climate was the top issue for 21 per cent of respondents.

The poll also suggested the Liberals’ track record on climate might be driving one in six Liberal voters to the NDP. The poll found climate was the top concern for half of NDP supporters.

The Canadian Research Insights Council, an industry organization that promotes polling standards, says online surveys cannot be assigned a margin of error because they do not randomly sample the population 

Aside from the political repercussions of publicly abandoning its commitment to the 2030 emission targets, Stewart said there are also legal implications.

The federal government is fighting a lawsuit brought by a group of climate advocates over Canada’s trajectory on emission commitments. The lawsuit is asking the Federal Court to order Ottawa to bring its 2030 emissions reductions plan into compliance with the Net-Zero Accountability Act.

“The courts can order the government to do something,” said Julia Levin, the associate director of national climate with Environmental Defence, one of the organizations behind the lawsuit.

“There is a clear consequence to that. But it is mostly political.”

Levin said climate change has become a point of political vulnerability for the Liberals.

“The prime minister knows this, and that’s why he’s done everything to dismantle the 2030 target. But I think it’s the reason that they won’t actually admit that they’ve abandoned this target,” Levin said.

“Internationally, this is a prime minister who cares deeply about his international reputation. And it’s hard to claim middle-power status and moral authority when you’ve abandoned a target that your peers are way more committed to.”

An analysis last year by the think tank 440 Megatonnes found Canada was the worst performer among G7 countries at reducing emissions compared to 2005 levels. All other G7 countries had an average reduction of 32 per cent by 2023, while Canada had only achieved 8.5 per cent.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 21, 2026

The post All signs show Canada can’t meet its Paris target — here’s why Ottawa won’t admit it appeared first on CHEK.

A new mini pharmacy in the remote Ahousaht First Nation community of Maaqtusiis on Flores Island is a game changer for its 1,200 residents.

]]>

Maaqtusiis, B.C. – A new mini pharmacy in the remote Ahousaht First Nation community of Maaqtusiis on Flores Island is a game changer for its 1,200 residents.

Now, when people fall acutely unwell, the mini pharmacy eliminates the cost of return boat travel and the wait time between leaving Ahousaht, reaching the nearest pharmacy in Tofino and returning home. On a blue bird day, it takes the water taxi 30-minutes to reach Tofino’s First Street Dock from Maaqtusiis. 

Officially launched on November 18 with an elder’s luncheon and naming ceremony, Ahousaht’s mini pharmacy or ʔuy̓aatłʔas (pronounced Oot-yaalth-us and translates to ‘a place where you’re given medicine’) is the second of its kind to exist in the Vancouver Island Health Region; the other is in Kingcome Inlet with Dzawada’enuxw First Nation, a place only accessible by boat or floatplane.

West Coast family physician Dr. George Saczek skippers his own boat from Tofino to the Chah Chum Hii Yup Tiic Mis health clinic on Flores Island for weekly rounds. He is currently the only doctor visiting Ahousaht. 

Dr. Saczek shared that in 2018 when he first started visiting Ahousaht, a sick baby came in to Chah Chum Hii Yup with a respiratory infection commonly known as croup. 

“I had nothing to give the baby. All that was available was a 45-minute boat ride,” said Dr. Saczek. “Usually, you would give the patients steroids right way, now we have an EpiPen inhaler.” 

“It might be a small pharmacy, but it’s making a big impact. I’ve already used up a lot of medication. Just within the first week of having it, we are at the point where we are having to re-stock things. It was something that was needed. From a physician perspective, I am extremely grateful I can help patients right away,” Dr. Saczek continued.

Erica Keen is the clinical manager for the ʔuukʷinkpanac – West Coast Primary Care Initiative (WCPCI) health team, a relatively new health services provider that offers primary care to people living in the central Nuu-chah-nulth communities of Ahousaht, Hot Springs Cove, Opitsaht, Ty-Histanis, Esowista, Hitacu and Macoah. 

With guidance from Ahousaht First Nation leadership, Keen says WCPCI consulted Vancouver Island Health Authority and First Nations Health Authority to make decisions around the mini pharmacy. 

“ʔuy̓aatłʔas is available to members who make appointments through (Dr. Saczek) or a PCI nurse. There are over 95 western medications that you can access. This is amazing. We are also learning as we go. If there are other ones that are missing, we can add, or that aren’t being used, we can cut out,” said Keen, noting that medications are supplied by Island Health.

Ahousaht’s mini pharmacy initiative is “decades in the making”, says Keen, and the project originated from “many, many years ago” when elder Dave Frank was the manager of the health centre. 

Frank is now a healer with Uut Uuštukyuu Society, a non-profit that facilitates access to Indigenous medicine in both reserve and urban communities across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland.

During the elder’s luncheon, Frank thanked the team from the Ahousaht and WCPCI for coming together to make the mini pharmacy real. He shared that there will be room for Indigenous medicines in the ʔuy̓aatłʔas as well. 

“We have medicine makers here in Ahousaht that are going to contribute. It doesn’t cost anything from us. Our kuu-us (First Nations) medicines are always free. When you get it from here, you don’t have to pay and you get instructions on how to use it,” said Frank. 

He went on the thank Myrtle Atleo and Walter Thomas, managers of the Chah Chum Hii Yup Tich Miss, for naming the space.

“Thank you for putting a spirit in the place. It’s important that we do that. Our ancestors would have done that,” said Frank. 

Tanille Johnston, Indigenous Health director for Island Health North Island region, said the mini pharmacy will bring a better quality of life to the residents of Maaqtusiis. 

“When we have strong and trusting relationships we can do beautiful things. This work of bringing pharmacy access closer to home is how we can demonstrate our vision of care for everyone, everywhere, every time,” said Johnston in a WCPCI press release.

WCPIC says this partnership represents a blueprint for other rural and remote First Nation communities who may want to open a mini pharmacy in their health centers. 

“A future goal is to incorporate traditional medicines into the mini pharmacy. We welcome anyone in Maaqtusiis to make an appointment to see doctors and primary care nurses and uut uustukyuu providers,” said WCPIC.

Currently, the mini pharmacy stocks diabetes medications, drugs for acute pain, antibiotic starter packs, birth control options and more. It is guarded with a lock and code, and it is not stocked with any opioids or benzos.

WCPCI is hiring for a pharmacist to serve all their partnering Nuu-chah-nulth communities, which include: Hesquiaht, Ahousaht, Tla-o-qui-aht, Ucluelet and Toquaht.

]]> 1363195 Doctors call for Port Hardy to become a permanent overnight ER following death https://cheknews.ca/doctors-call-for-port-hardy-to-become-a-permanent-overnight-er-following-death-1363197/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 01:46:26 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363197

After a woman's death at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday, doctors are proposing to turn the ER department into a permanent overnight site.

The post Doctors call for Port Hardy to become a permanent overnight ER following death appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

After a woman’s death at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday, doctors are proposing to turn the ER department into a permanent overnight site.

Since 2023, Port Hardy residents have dealt with the harsh reality that their only emergency room within 40 kilometres closes every night from 5 p.m. to 7 a.m.

The ongoing overnight closures are a result of staffing shortages, according to Island Health.

On Thursday night, a woman arrived at the hospital after 5 p.m., when the ER was closed. At 5:11 p.m., BCEHS says paramedics learned of the patient’s presence and began treating her in the parking lot.

Eventually, she was brought inside to be treated by staff but was later pronounced dead.

“We’ve grown numb to this; it’s terrible. It’s terrible that it takes a tragic outcome, a death, to shake us from our numbness,” said Dr. Alex Nataros.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Nataros is the founder of the North Island Community Health Centre and has long criticized Island Health’s handling of the staffing shortage at the hospital. His colleague was involved in the attempts to save the woman’s life.

He sees this death as related to the ongoing closures.

“We’ve had over 30 walk-in patients today, and a number have raised concerns,” said Naratos.

“Having organizations like Island Health, full of managers and ‘Yes’ men, that agree to work and don’t improve the underlying problems leads to unnecessary deaths. I can count the deaths, and it’s terrible. Change is urgently needed.”

On Saturday, Island Health had no new update, referring CHEK News to information provided on Friday.

“We are reviewing the circumstances of this case with BC Emergency Health Services and it would be inappropriate to speculate on any factors that may have contributed while that review is underway,” said the health authority on Friday.

“What we can say at this time, based on initial review and follow-up, is that both Island Health care providers and BCEHS paramedics responded and provided emergency interventions.”

The ongoing overnight closures are sparking calls from North Island doctors to turn the Port Hardy ER into a permanent overnight regional emergency department. Naratos shared a letter to CHEK News that he says doctors have signed on to.

The letter says the Port McNeill hospital, roughly 43 kilometres from Port Hardy, has disproportionately taken on the burden for overnight ER coverage. Despite investments for the region, the ongoing staffing shortage continues to prevent the ER from opening 24/7, according to the letter.

“It has become clear to the local physicians that the safest and most sustainable long-term solution is to designate a single ER as the overnight site for the region permanently,” reads the letter.

Doctors want Port Hardy to become that site because of population size, patient volume, and acuity of calls.

“It’s a much sicker population, we’re also nearly double the size, and we have three First Nation reserves adjacent,” said Naratos.

He’s calling on the newly elected B.C. Government to take action for a situation that has long been dire.

Naratos says he spoke with North Island MLA Anna Kindy on Saturday.

“We spoke for over 20 minutes, and she gave me a clear commitment that her first job Monday morning is to get on the phone with Premier Lorne Doerkson and turn this ship around.”

“My heart goes out to the family and loved ones of the woman who died after arriving at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday night, and to the paramedics, doctors and staff who fought to save her,” said MLA Anna Kindy in a statement.

“Minutes matter in an emergency, and our government is deeply committed to strengthening those services for people in every part of our province.”

Health Minister Ryan Peterson tells CHEK News in a statement that access to health care is a top priority and that he will work with all parties to ensure the findings of the review into the woman’s death lead to more reliable emergency care.

With files from CHEK’s Kori Sidaway
